findings.title: The run ad8c3ce4 adds after every order reads spent leaves the page saying "Waiting for the order to fill … Stop cancels it." and keeps Stop, whose dialog describes and prices a cancel that never happens
findings.scenario:
The user swaps 10 ₳ for MIN, through Lovejoin by default, and a batcher fills the order. The first run that reads the order spent (a Refresh, the page's 20 s poll, or the alarm) now only records auto.spentSeen and returns. Until the next run past READ_EVERY_MS:
- The page says "Waiting for the order to fill. Then it all comes back by itself; Stop cancels it."
- Home and the swaps list say "Running · Waiting for the fill".
- The Stop button stays.

Stop's dialog says "The order is cancelled, unless it fills first, and everything comes back to your private balance. Its ADA goes through Lovejoin first: at most 2 boxes of 5 ₳, about 1.9 ₳ in mix fees and 0.6 ₳ to bring them back, each after 1 to 6 hours. The cancel costs a network fee too." None of that happens: there is no cancel, and the same account prices 0 boxes once the fill is told. For a MIN→ADA swap the dialog prices 0 boxes, so there's no Lovejoin switch and it says everything comes back. The return then mixes 6 boxes. Pressing Stop builds no cancel. Its own step tells the outcome and sends the first return at once. Nothing is lost.

A stopped swap marked "Order open" keeps that line and tag for the extra pass too, because the noted run returns before noteOrderOpen(false).

What the page should say in that step is what it says once a fill or refund is read: "It all comes back to your private balance next, by itself.", with no Stop, as flows.md:480 has it ("Stop, there until the order is filled or refunded").

How long the step lasts in use is one more pass:
- The page open: its next 20 s poll, about 20 s (up to about 35 s after a Refresh). A second Refresh tells it at once.
- The page closed: the sessions alarm, up to about 1 min while unlocked.
- Home's 20 s read only reads the device's record, so it never moves the step on.
- Locked: nothing runs until the next unlock. That run tells the outcome, and the return then waits the unlock's draw (20 min at most).

The e2e at extension.spec.ts:2947-2948 does one Refresh and expects the return, so it fails on both builds.
findings.evidence:
Lines are FIXTREE's (ad8c3ce4).
- sessions.ts:3986-3991: `if (auto.spentSeen === undefined) { await this.update(network, s.index, (r) => { r.auto!.spentSeen = now(); }); return; }`. It returns before filled/refunded are written (:3999-4007) and before `s = await this.noteOrderOpen(network, s, false)` (:4022).
- autoView (sessions.ts:6729-6770) never reads spentSeen. The view is step "filling" ("cancelling" once stopping), filled false, no refunded, and orderOpen is kept while cancelling.
- Swaps.tsx:3341-3344 nowLine: `if (a.filled || a.refunded || a.againstPools) return t("swaps.now.comingBackNext"); return t("swaps.now.filling");`.
- Swaps.tsx:325-330 stoppable is `!a.stopping && !a.filled && !a.refunded && !a.againstPools && (… || a.step === "filling")`. So Stop renders (:2508), and stopReading (:342) gives over false, so the dialog stays open.
- sessions.ts:3513 stopCost: `const out = !!sent && !auto.filled && !auto.refunded;`. With :3544-3548 it prices a cancel's refund of the funded ADA for an ADA-in swap, and 0 for a token-in swap.
- Timing:
  - READ_EVERY_MS 15_000 (sessions.ts:254) throttles every run but "asked" (:3738).
  - The page polls session-advance with now:false every ADVANCE_EVERY_MS 20_000 (Swaps.tsx:2108, :2203).
  - The sessions alarm runs every minute while unlocked (sw.ts:87 periodInMinutes 1; runs.ts:50-53 stops it when locked).
  - Home reads `sessions` every 20 s (Home.tsx:427-455). That is list(network, false) (sessions.ts:1584), the record only, and steps nothing.

findings.fix:
Carry the noted step into the view and treat it on screen as a fill or refund already read:
- autoView gives `spent: true` while auto.spentSeen is set and neither filled nor refunded is.
- nowLine: in filling and cancelling, `a.spent` reads swaps.now.comingBackNext.
- stoppable, and so stopReading's `over`: false with `a.spent`, so Stop goes.

- The noted run calls noteOrderOpen(network, s, false) before it returns.

- architecture.md:649 and :667 still say the outcome is decided in the run that reads every order spent. They should say it's told by the next run.
- Add a Vitest of the noted view's words, Stop and stopCost, as l3s-spentseen.test.ts does.

findings.title: Where 7b6881f7 meets ad8c3ce4: a late leg's direct return now writes the session's skip reason, and the last step says "Directly: Lovejoin was left out" under its link to the swap's own return, which went through Lovejoin
findings.scenario:
MIN is sold for ADA through Lovejoin, and Minswap splits it into two orders. Leg 2's fill is in no listing until the swap's first return, a 7-transaction chain, has gone. lovejoin-planner.test.ts's second r2still#2 case builds exactly this.

ad8c3ce4 counts that leg as the swap's own, so the direct return that brings it back writes NO_COLLATERAL as the session's lovejoinSkipped. privacy.md:458 wants that reason said in the callout. But backStepText puts lovejoinSkipped ahead of 7b6881f7's own-return rule. So the finished swap's last step, Back in your private balance, says "Directly: Lovejoin was left out", while its link (7b6881f7) opens the first return, the chain's.

Nothing on the page still says that boxes come back later, each by itself. The Received row shows what came back at once, short of the boxes' ADA, with no word that the boxes are still to come. flows.md:478 (7b6881f7) promises the step says how the first return came back: "a later one never takes its place there, nor a chain sent after it, nor why Lovejoin was left out of it". No money is lost: the boxes come back on their waits.

findings.title: ad8c3ce4's landedAfter dates a stranger's payment against the swap's chain's last transaction: a payment landing while that chain is sent reads as the swap's own, and its skip reason takes over the swap's page (e2b#2 again)
findings.scenario:
A MIN→ADA swap is filled, and everything of it is listed. Its return's chain is built from the account at T and sent a block at a time, which takes minutes, or longer while its collateral's mix waits for giveme.my. Its last transaction, the return, goes out at T+2 min.

At T+1 min a stranger pays the session's one-time account 20 ₳. The account's address has been public since its funding. Device and chain clocks agree.

A second return brings the 20 ₳ back. landedAfter compares the row's block time with firstBack.at, which for a chain is when its last transaction was sent. So the stranger's row "landed before" the return, isn't strangers-only, and its NO_COLLATERAL reason becomes the session's word. The finished swap's page shows "Lovejoin was left out of its return: its 5 ₳ collateral isn't at its account anymore, and the mixes need it…" and a last step of "Directly: Lovejoin was left out". The swap's own money came back through Lovejoin. This is e2b#2's symptom, which round one fixed.

Under round one's rule (landedAfter dropped, in a scratch copy), the same run keeps no reason, and the step reads "What goes into Lovejoin boxes comes back later, each box by itself; the rest at once, under fresh registers". A device clock running ahead widens the window. One running behind reads a real late leg as a stranger's, which brings r2still#2's residual back. Words only, nothing moves.

findings.fix:
Tell a leg of the swap by what its transaction spends, not by time. A row whose transaction spends one of the swap's recorded orders (the landed swap's `orders`) is a fill or a refund, and anything else is a stranger's. That takes one tx_info, with inputs, for the rows that are neither own nor fills, asked only when a later return is built.

Failing that, date the first return from when it was built from its listing: the first transaction of its chain, or s.chain.at for a chain, never the chain's last send. Give that comparison the house's clock margin in the direction that keeps e2b#2. r2still#2's verifier also offered "a block above where it landed".

sendChain's `if (strangers) return;` takes the same rule. Pin it with the probe above, expecting no skip reason and the throughLovejoin step, beside lovejoin-planner's r2still#2 cases.
